criteria.title: Souls UI bootstraps from relay data and stays live with soul updates
criteria.assertion: The Souls browser experience must load soul and template data from relay-backed events, order the resulting collections deterministically for display, and keep the visible soul collection updated from live `31951` events after bootstrap.
preconditions: The browser has relay connectivity and a Soul Factory pubkey / author context.
Relay responses contain at least one template or soul event for the bootstrap case.
steps: Load the Souls gallery and template list from relay-backed queries.
Deliver a live `31951` update for an existing soul and for a newly discovered soul.
criteria.expected_result: Bootstrap renders the relay-backed collections, templates are available for provisioning flows, and live soul events update or insert visible soul state without requiring a page reload.
negative_cases: If the browser depends on a REST route instead of relay-backed soul/template queries for this feature, the criterion fails.
If live soul updates are ignored after bootstrap, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Browser provisioning requests are signer-first and explicitly tagged
criteria.assertion: Creating a soul from the browser must require signer-backed auth, publish a signed `5950` request with explicit `agent-id`, `name`, `tier`, and optional `template` tags, include the provisioning brief in content, and fail locally when no relay accepts the publish.
preconditions: A user has access to a browser signing surface.
A relay is configured for the request publish path.
steps: Attempt provisioning without signer availability.
Attempt provisioning with a signer and valid request fields.
Attempt provisioning when every relay rejects or fails the publish.
criteria.expected_result: Unsigned provisioning is blocked, valid requests are signed and published with the required tags/content, and zero-accept publish attempts fail rather than reporting provisioning success.
negative_cases: If the browser can publish a provisioning request without a signer-backed identity, the criterion fails.
If a request missing required tags is treated as valid request output, the criterion fails.
If zero accepted relay publishes still transition the UI into a successful provisioning state, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: The reactor rejects unauthorized or malformed provisioning requests with correlated terminal errors
criteria.assertion: The Soul Factory reactor must reject unauthorized requesters and malformed `5950` payloads, and must publish a correlated `7950` error result that references the original request event and requester instead of silently accepting or dropping the request.
preconditions: The reactor is running with an authorized-provisioner configuration.
A requester can publish provisioning requests to the subscribed relays.
steps: Publish a `5950` request from an unauthorized pubkey.
Publish malformed `5950` requests that omit required data such as `agent-id` or any brief/template/draft source.
criteria.expected_result: Each rejected request yields a correlated terminal `7950` error result describing the failure reason, and no soul is provisioned.
negative_cases: If unauthorized requesters can provision souls, the criterion fails.
If malformed requests are accepted without a correlated terminal error, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Successful provisioning follows the documented eight-step event-driven workflow
criteria.assertion: A successful provisioning run must progress through the documented generate, Signet, avatar, profile, Qdrant, memory, workspace, and deploy/finalize stages, emit correlated `6950` progress for meaningful steps, and end with a correlated `7950` success result rather than implicit completion.
preconditions: A valid provisioning request has been accepted.
A non-placeholder provisioning engine is configured.
steps: Execute a successful provisioning run from accepted `5950` request through completion.
Observe correlated progress and terminal result events plus recorded run state.
criteria.expected_result: The run records eight ordered stages, emits progress/status during provisioning, and ends only when a correlated terminal result is published.
negative_cases: If provisioning reports completion without a terminal correlated `7950` result, the criterion fails.
If a configured successful run skips mandatory stages without explicit skipped/failure accounting, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Provisioning outputs are truthful about optional integration success, failure, and skip states
criteria.assertion: Soul Factory must only claim avatar, vector-memory, agent-memory, workspace, NIP-05, snapshot, or deployment-related outputs that were actually produced; when optional integrations are unconfigured or fail non-fatally, the run must explicitly record skipped or failed step state instead of inventing successful outputs.
preconditions: Provisioning is executed once with optional adapters absent and once with at least one optional step failing non-fatally.
steps: Run provisioning with optional adapters unconfigured.
Run provisioning where an optional integration fails after provisioning has begun.
Inspect step results and final soul outputs.
criteria.expected_result: Skipped or failed optional steps are explicit in run state, and the final soul omits outputs that were not actually produced.
negative_cases: If an unconfigured optional step still populates synthetic avatar, workspace, vector-memory, or related outputs, the criterion fails.
If optional-step failure is hidden as success, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Successful provisioning publishes an authoritative `31951` soul that the browser can consume
criteria.assertion: After successful provisioning, Soul Factory must publish a `31951` soul event containing the soul’s replaceable identity coordinate and authoritative metadata needed for downstream visibility, and the browser must be able to surface that published soul through normal relay-backed reads or live updates.
preconditions: A provisioning run has completed successfully.
steps: Observe the published `31951` event after successful provisioning.
Reload or live-update the Souls browser view against the relevant relays.
criteria.expected_result: The `31951` event includes authoritative soul identity/state fields, and the provisioned soul becomes discoverable in the browser experience without extra side channels.
negative_cases: If successful provisioning completes without publishing a `31951` soul event, the criterion fails.
If the browser cannot consume the published soul through the relay-backed flow, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Provisioned souls must integrate with Bahia deployment state end to end when Bahia integration is configured
criteria.assertion: When Bahia integration is configured, a successfully provisioned soul must be registered as a Bahia service, receive initial deployment hookup for the configured agent environment, and expose deploy-status visibility that can be reflected back into the soul’s published state.
preconditions: Bahia integration is configured with a registry and agent environment.
A provisioning run completes successfully.
steps: Provision a soul with Bahia integration enabled.
Inspect service registration, deployment-hookup behavior, and resulting deploy-status visibility in soul state.
criteria.expected_result: The provisioned soul is represented as a Bahia-managed service, initial deployment integration occurs for the configured environment, and soul state can surface deployment status rather than remaining disconnected from Bahia.
negative_cases: If the soul registers as a service but never gains initial deployment hookup for the configured environment, the criterion fails.
If deploy-status visibility cannot be surfaced back into soul state when Bahia integration is configured, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Lifecycle actions are signer-first, authorized, and correlated to the target soul
criteria.assertion: Suspend, resume, revoke, redeploy, and regenerate operations must be initiated as signed `1950` soul-action events that explicitly reference the target soul and action type, and unauthorized or malformed actions must fail rather than mutating state silently.
preconditions: A target soul exists.
An initiator can attempt signed and unsigned or unauthorized action publishes.
steps: Publish valid signed lifecycle actions for an existing soul.
Attempt malformed or unauthorized lifecycle actions.
criteria.expected_result: Valid actions are correlated to the target soul and processed; malformed or unauthorized actions are rejected without silent state mutation.
negative_cases: If an action can mutate soul state without explicit soul/action correlation, the criterion fails.
If unauthorized lifecycle actions succeed, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Suspend, resume, revoke, and redeploy must propagate both soul-state and managed-runtime effects
criteria.assertion: For Bahia-managed souls, suspend, resume, revoke, and redeploy must do more than publish local soul-state changes: they must also propagate the corresponding managed deployment and agent-access side effects, and the resulting soul/action state must reflect the completed lifecycle outcome.
preconditions: A Bahia-managed soul exists.
Lifecycle action handlers and downstream integrations are active.
steps: Execute suspend, resume, revoke, and redeploy actions against a managed soul in separate runs.
Inspect resulting soul state, action-result signaling, and managed deployment / access side effects.
criteria.expected_result: Each lifecycle action updates soul state and causes the corresponding managed effect rather than stopping at a UI-only or event-only acknowledgment.
negative_cases: If lifecycle actions report completion while Bahia-managed deployment state remains unchanged, the criterion fails.
If revoke completes without the expected termination or access-revocation side effects, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Regenerate must require a new brief and republish revised soul identity content
criteria.assertion: Regenerating a soul must require a new brief, regenerate the soul’s identity content from that brief, republish the updated soul state, and publish a correlated action result that reflects the regeneration outcome.
preconditions: An existing soul is available for regeneration.
A signed regenerate action can be published.
steps: Publish a regenerate action without a new brief.
Publish a regenerate action with a valid new brief.
Inspect the resulting soul publication and action result.
criteria.expected_result: Missing-brief regenerate attempts fail; valid regenerate attempts produce updated soul content and a correlated completion result.
negative_cases: If regenerate succeeds without a new brief, the criterion fails.
If a successful regenerate does not republish updated soul content, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Soul Factory CLI commands must perform real Nostr-backed query and mutation flows
criteria.assertion: The Soul Factory CLI surface must support list, get, provision, suspend, resume, revoke, redeploy, regenerate, and template commands through real signed Nostr publish/query behavior rather than returning explicit unavailability stubs.
preconditions: CLI auth/signing and relay connectivity are configured.
steps: Run each supported Soul Factory CLI command against a configured environment.
Inspect whether it performs real query or signed publish work.
criteria.expected_result: Each command executes the intended Soul Factory operation using real Nostr-backed behavior and returns real results or real correlated failures from the underlying system.
negative_cases: If a supported CLI command still returns the current explicit unavailability stub, the criterion fails.
If a CLI command simulates success without real publish/query work, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Soul Factory MCP tools must perform real query, mutation, and status flows
criteria.assertion: The Soul Factory MCP surface must support real list/get/template/provision/action/regenerate/status behavior through actual query, signed publish, and correlated status/result flows rather than static unavailability responses.
preconditions: An MCP caller can invoke Soul Factory tools against a configured environment.
steps: Invoke the Soul Factory MCP tools for querying, provisioning, lifecycle action, regeneration, and status retrieval.
Inspect whether the tools perform real query or mutation work and expose real run status.
criteria.expected_result: The MCP surface returns real query data, can initiate real provisioning and lifecycle operations, and exposes real provisioning status rather than configuration-level unavailability errors.
negative_cases: If list/template/provision/action/regenerate tools still return explicit unavailability messages instead of real work, the criterion fails.
If MCP status cannot reflect real provisioning runs, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Browser provisioning tracking must remain event-driven and non-terminal until correlated result or explicit rejection
criteria.assertion: The browser’s provisioning-run tracker must not treat elapsed local time or relay-subscription closure by itself as the normative terminal failure signal for a provisioning run; terminal success or failure must remain correlated to explicit provisioning result semantics or explicit pre-acceptance publish rejection.
preconditions: A browser provisioning run has been started.
The test can simulate missing progress, delayed results, and relay closure conditions.
steps: Start provisioning tracking for a request that does not immediately receive a terminal result.
Simulate elapsed time and subscription closure before a correlated terminal result arrives.
Simulate explicit publish rejection and explicit correlated terminal error result cases.
criteria.expected_result: Explicit publish rejection and explicit correlated terminal result events can conclude the run; elapsed time or subscription closure alone are not treated as the approved terminal contract behavior.
negative_cases: If the browser still marks a provisioning run terminally failed solely because a local timer elapsed, the criterion fails.
If relay closure alone is treated as the normative terminal failure result, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Bahia-to-soul deploy-status propagation must use event-driven synchronization rather than ticker polling
criteria.assertion: Soul deploy-status updates sourced from Bahia must propagate into soul state through event-driven synchronization behavior, and the approved product contract for this feature must not depend on ticker-based polling as the normal mechanism for keeping soul deploy status current.
preconditions: A Bahia-managed soul exists and Bahia emits deployment-state changes relevant to that soul.
steps: Trigger deployment-state changes for a Bahia-managed soul.
Observe how soul deploy status is synchronized and republished.
criteria.expected_result: Soul deploy-status updates are driven by explicit Bahia event changes and republished into soul state without depending on ticker polling as the approved synchronization contract.
negative_cases: If ticker polling remains the required or normative mechanism for deploy-status freshness, the criterion fails.
If Bahia deployment-state changes cannot be reflected back into soul state without polling, the criterion fails.
